prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1313; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a low-speed head-on collision at an intersection. Insured vehicle and third-party vehicle both sustained front-end damage. Claimant reports neck and lower back discomfort following the impact and says she was seen at an urgent care facility the same day. No attorney involved at this time; claimant is communicating directly. Photos of both vehicles requested.

Entry 2: Received photos from insured and claimant. Front bumper damage on both vehicles appears consistent with a low-speed impact. Airbag did not deploy in either vehicle per police report. Recorded statement taken from insured, who confirms the other driver crossed into the oncoming lane while turning. Liability appears to lean toward the other driver, pending review.

Entry 3: Spoke with claimant by phone. She describes a dull ache in the lower back that worsens after sitting for long periods. Medical report from urgent care lists a lumbar strain with prescribed rest and over-the-counter pain relief. Explained the claims process and the documentation I will need. Claimant stated she has not hired a lawyer and prefers to handle the claim herself.

Entry 4: Obtained the independent appraisal for the claimant's vehicle. Repair estimate is under review and a supplement may be needed for hidden frame damage. Requested the claimant's treatment records and a list of missed work days, if any. Claimant agreed to send them by email this week.

Entry 5: Follow-up call with claimant. She reports the back strain is improving with physical therapy referral she has scheduled. Confirmed the bodily injury portion of the claim remains open until treatment concludes. Advised claimant to keep receipts for any out-of-pocket medical costs. Next review set for the coming week once the records arrive.
